title: Assessing mentalization in humans and large language models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26291v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Mentalization - the ability to infer others' beliefs and intentions to guide one's own choices - is a key cognitive function underlying human social interactions. Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate behaviour consistent with humans on theory-of-mind tasks, yet whether these models can guide adaptive behaviour through mentalization is unknown. Here we use two economic games with cognitive computational modeling to uncover the latent strategies underlying mentalization in LLMs. We tested individual LLM agents across four model families, DeepSeek, GPT-4.1, GPT-5 and Gemini 2.0 Flash (N = 2,099), against opponents of varying sophistication and examined whether a prompting strategy designed to elicit strategic reasoning improved performance. translated_title: 评估人类与大型语言模型中的心理化能力
translated_abstract: 心理化——推断他人信念和意图以指导自身选择的能力——是人类社会互动中的关键认知功能。大型语言模型（LLMs）在心理理论任务上表现出与人类一致的行为，但这些模型能否通过心理化来指导适应性行为尚不清楚。在此，我们使用两个经济博弈和认知计算建模来揭示LLMs中心理化背后的潜在策略。我们测试了来自四个模型家族（DeepSeek、GPT-4.1、GPT-5和Gemini 2.0 Flash，N = 2,099）的个体LLM代理，针对不同复杂度的对手，并考察了旨在激发策略性推理的提示策略是否能提高性能。我们将结果与人类参与者（N = 251）进行基准比较。在两个博弈中，LLMs均表现出明显的心理化行为和计算特征，且这些特征存在显著差异。
tldr: 本研究通过经济博弈和计算建模证明，大型语言模型在心理化能力上展现出与人类相似但存在显著差异的行为和计算特征，且提示策略可提升其策略推理表现。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that large language models exhibit mentalization-like behavioral and computational signatures distinct from humans in economic games, with prompting strategies enhancing their strategic reasoning.
